title: KBoC Necromancer
subtitle: KBoC early leveling and progression guide

content.text: This guide pulls its resources from a mixture of
YT videos + google sheets and personal experience playing this build over last 3 leagues.
What this build is good at

: highly excels at fast mapping and content such as Breach, Legion, Blight or anything that needs to kill a lot and spread wide. Single target is high once you invest. Right out of maps you have decent life and ES pool with eventual swap to CI with capped block, over 7K ES pool, 12k armor, great movement and excellent recovery. Probably one of the best all-rounder builds over the last few leagues that can do all content around 20-30 divines and scale into hundreds of divines if you want.
for the entire campaign then swapping to KBoC in maps where you can then follow the excellent guides from legi and redviles linked below.

content.text: : Act 6 is where you decide if you want to keep leveling with
set up. Since I only play SC Trade,
and purchase KBoC from trade for A10/Maps swap. Around hour 3-4 of league start most trans gems are a few chaos, KBoC included, and it'll be the literal first purchase I make.

The 2 most popular creators (Redviles & Legi) who I stole this guide from, both swap from KBolt (A1) > KF (A2-A5) > KB (A6-Early maps) > KBoC. I am a shitter and prefer the 2 IQ route so KF just makes sense to me until I buy KBoC, because fuck doing labs.

Also note, you can literally play KF with SSF campaign gear deep into yellow maps with relative ease on a 5 link, so feel free farm up a few chaos if you need or just enter lab prison till you get KBoC. I have personally tested this in 3.29 in SSF for practice.
If you decide to stick to KF for campaign the only thing that changes is addition of
to gem links. The tree stays identical for both KF and KB leveling methods.
Take these tree nodes as you fit. I'd recommend the leech nodes first to help with sustain but after that it's up to you.
If you need more general damage take the accuracy, if you need more single target take the mark, if you need life take the life, up to you on the order.

content.text: Notes below are stolen from Redviles' video, go watch that for a more in depth explanation on everything. You should be following anyways, dude is insane.
Typically right out of campaign you play

as a Phys to light conversion setup since it's the cheaper route. That's why you'll see a lot of conversion nodes on the tree and the gem as a 5th link. However, if it's cheap enough to swap to Chaos version (Medium cluster required) then you can skip all of that and follow the notes below. This is most likely what I will do and is what Redviles did in 3.29.

Enables the Arcanist Brand triple-curse setup, providing roughly 50% more damage against cursed targets without slowing down your KB ramp-up like totems do. Overall, this can provide over 70% more damage against the branded target.
Prioritize mana, critical strike chance, and attack speed on a Kinetic Wand. Spell damage, crit multi, and chaos penetration are good bonus mods.

Get endurance charge generation early. Options include:

Prioritize both life and energy shield on gear, with a greater focus on ES.
for ES leech. You'll still have life recovery on kill and a life flask.
Prioritize mana prefixes on gloves and boots.
Don't facetank everything yet! The build is naturally squishier before CI. Use your extremely fast Shield Charge to dodge boss attacks and spells.

Only use Shavronne's ring after switching to CI, otherwise you'll run into mana issues.
